**The scope mismatch (the crux):**

| Source | What it says |
|---|---|
| Diane's email summary (6/29) | Heat exchanger failing + thermocouple out, "tank held pressure on hold test" → exchanger swap + new thermocouple, **~$310**, Thursday AM |
| Tony's Slack endorsement (6/29) | Same — exchanger swap only, ~$310, "tank tested sound," keeps Robert on June budget |

**Scope landed: full water heater replacement, not the $310 patch.**

Before signing off for Hill Country's Thursday AM slot, I went back to the diagnostic write-up on the bill itself (Hill Country B2026-211) and checked it against the summary Diane emailed and Tony endorsed. They don't line up:

- **Summary in circulation (Diane's email + Tony's Slack):** heat exchanger failing + thermocouple out, "tank held pressure / tested sound" → exchanger swap + new thermocouple, ~$310, keeps us on Robert's June budget.
- **Diagnostic on the bill:** 12-yr Ruud RS75, corrosion on the burner assembly **and tank base**, thermocouple out, **cracked heat exchanger**. Hill Country's own written recommendation is **full unit replacement (~$1,850, equal-model swap)**, and it explicitly states **piecemeal repair is not advised on a unit this age**.

The $310 scope is exactly the patch the diagnostic advises against, and it leaves the corroded tank base untouched. Last night's call — no hot water since 4 PM, water spreading across the kitchen floor, kids back home — reads like tank/base failure, not an exchanger-only fault, and contradicts the "tank held pressure" note.

**Decision:** move on the full replacement. Priority bumped to Urgent for the active leak + no hot water. Hill Country to pull a replacement Ruud RS75 (equal model) for Thursday 07-02 AM; parts pull requested today. Airtable MT-2026-1327 updated to match. Robert Finley getting a cost heads-up since this is well above the ~$310 patch and the June budget assumption.

input.subject: Mesa Vista Unit 7B — water heater update and this week's timing
input.body:
Hi Tanya,

Thanks for calling last night and letting me know the water heater had gotten worse — no hot water and water spreading on the kitchen floor, with the kids back home. I'm sorry you're dealing with that.

Here's where things landed and what to expect this week. Our plumber's diagnostic showed the heater (an older unit) has a cracked internal part plus corrosion at the base of the tank, which is what's causing the leak. Rather than a partial patch that wouldn't hold on a unit this age, we're going to replace the whole water heater so this is fixed properly and you're not back to a leaking tank in a few weeks.

Timing:
- Hill Country Plumbing is scheduled Thursday morning (7/2) to install the new unit. Please plan for their crew to have access to the water heater area that morning.
- I'll be onsite while they work.
- Hot water should be back the same day once the new unit is installed and tested.

In the meantime, if the leak worsens or you see water reaching outlets or spreading further, call me right away and, if you can do so safely, you can shut off the water supply valve to the heater to slow the leak. Please keep the area around it clear so the crew can get right to work Thursday.

I'll follow up to confirm the exact arrival window once the plumber locks it in. Thanks for your patience — we'll get this taken care of.

Best,
Carlos Mendez
Star Property Management

input.subject: Mesa Vista Unit 7B — water heater replacement, cost heads-up
input.body:
Hi Robert,

A quick heads-up on a repair at Mesa Vista Unit 7B (Tanya's unit). What started as a small drip earlier this week turned into a full failure last night — the tenant lost hot water entirely and water was spreading across the kitchen floor, with children in the home, so this is now a time-sensitive habitability item.

Hill Country Plumbing ran a diagnostic on the unit. It's a 12-year-old Ruud water heater with a cracked heat exchanger plus corrosion on both the burner assembly and the tank base. Their written recommendation is a full replacement (about $1,850 for an equal-model swap), and they specifically advise against a piecemeal repair on a unit this age.

There was an earlier, cheaper option floated — an exchanger-and-thermocouple patch at around $310 — but that scope didn't match the diagnostic: it left the corroded tank base untouched, and last night's leak points to the tank itself, not just the exchanger. A $310 patch would very likely leave you back here with a leaking tank shortly, so I'm not comfortable running it.

Given the active leak and loss of hot water, we're moving ahead with the full replacement in Hill Country's Thursday morning (7/2) slot. I wanted to flag the cost directly since it's well above the earlier ~$310 estimate and the June budget assumption. Happy to walk through it by phone if you'd like — otherwise I'll send confirmation once the work is completed.

Best,
Carlos Mendez
Star Property Management
